web_title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
book_title: Chapter 7: What Is Priced In — Normalized Excess Returns & Peer Valuation
question: What mid-cycle normalized ROAE is embedded in RenaissanceRe at $343.97 (1.42x Q3 2026 TBVPS, 1.32x BVPS, 8.10x forward P/E), and does it offer a margin of safety?

epigraph.quote: Paying 1.42 times tangible book for a cyclical reinsurer requires proof that mid-cycle returns exceed the cost of capital by a wide margin—never extrapolate benign catastrophe seasons forever.
epigraph.author: Insurance Valuation Discipline

web_blocks.title: 7.1 Reverse Valuation & Excess-Return Model on Mid-Cycle ROAE

web_blocks.html: At $343.97 on November 20, 2026, RenaissanceRe carries a $13.90 billion market cap [21]. Shares trade at 9.89x trailing earnings ($34.78 TTM EPS), 8.10x forward earnings, and 4.93x price-to-free-cash-flow [21]. Against audited Q3 2026 book value per share of $259.61 ($259.60 Finviz), the P/B ratio is 1.32x [3, 18, 21]. Against audited Q3 2026 tangible book value per share (TBVPS) of $242.51, the P/TBV ratio is 1.42x [3, 18]. Wall Street's average target sits at $349.94, just +1.7% above current price, with consensus projecting -14.48% EPS contraction next year [21]. Because catastrophe timing and mark-to-market bond swings distort industrial DCF models, we value RenRe using justified P/B and excess returns: P/B = (ROAE - g) / (CoE - g) [23].

Our cost of equity (CoE) must reflect current macro rates and balance-sheet risk. With the U.S. 10-year Treasury yielding 5.04% (2-year at 4.76%), a 5.46% catastrophe, duration, and reserve risk premium yields a 10.50% CoE [23, 28]. RenRe's low 0.12 equity beta measures stock correlation, not climate or social-inflation tail risk. Meanwhile, our forensic filing audit uncovered five structural drags that pull sustainable mid-cycle ROAE down to 12.0%–14.0%, well below the 20.3% annualized 9M 2026 figure [1, 3, 18]. First, Property Catastrophe gross premiums fell 19.9% YoY in 9M 2026 as ILS supply softened rates, while 2026's ultra-benign 31.2% Property combined ratio will revert toward normal 55%–62% budgets [3, 6, 12]. Second, Casualty & Specialty deteriorated to a 110.6% Q3 2026 combined ratio (104.7% 9M) with $54.66 million of adverse prior-year development [3, 17].

Three other frictions reinforce a 13.0% mid-cycle ROAE baseline (13.9% on tangible equity) [3, 18]. Capital Partners quarterly fees stepped down four consecutive quarters from $101.8 million to $81.7 million amid $649.2 million DaVinci and $140.9 million Fontana redemptions [3, 18]. Retained fixed-income duration stretched from 3.0 to 4.2 years on a trading-classified $25.20 billion bond book, driving $(1,180.1) million in 9M 2026 MTM losses alongside $1.60 billion in locked-up private credit funds [3, 18]. Also, Bermuda's 15% Corporate Income Tax imposes a permanent tax drag (~9.9% FY2025 consolidated ETR after JV exclusions), and both CFO Robert Qutub and CPO Ross Curtis retire on December 31, 2026 [1, 13]. Plugging 13.0% ROAE, 10.5% CoE, and 3.0% growth into justified P/B gives 1.333x on $259.61 BVPS, or $346.15 today—almost identical to CMP ($343.97) [18, 23]. Compounding $259.61 by +11.0% (13.0% ROAE less 0.5% dividend and 1.5% buyback dilution) yields $288.17 raw Q3 2027E BVPS; subtracting ~200 bps (~$5.17/share) for net fixed-maturity MTM drag and buyback-premium friction gives $283.00 (+9.01%, or ~$267.50 TBVPS after ~$1.60/share intangibles amortization) [3, 18]. Even at raw $288.17 x 1.29x = $371.74 (+8.1%), Base reward-to-risk is 1.04:1 at CMP (0.89:1 at $346.13), still failing our 1.50:1 hurdle [23].

web_blocks.takeaway: At a realistic 10.5% cost of equity (anchored by a 5.04% 10-year Treasury), a 13.0% mid-cycle ROAE yields 1.33x BVPS ($346), showing zero margin of safety at $343.97.

Applying a 1.29x justified P/B ((13.0% - 3.0%) / (10.5% - 3.0%) = 1.333x discounted for 110.6% Q3 casualty drag) gives $365.00 Base; even raw $288.17 x 1.29 = $371.74 still rejects at 1.04:1 Base R:R.
web_blocks.the_inputs: Audited Q3 2026 BVPS $259.61 and TBVPS $242.51; 13.0% mid-cycle ROAE (12%–14% band); 10.50% Cost of Equity (5.04% 10Y Treasury + 5.46% cat/duration ERP); 3.0% terminal growth; 8.10x forward P/E; 4.2-year retained fixed-income duration.
web_blocks.the_range: Bear $275.00 (30% prob: 10.0% ROAE, heavy cat + casualty creep -> 1.00x BVPS; stressed Red Team 10.0% ROAE at 0.9333x P/B + +100 bps rate MTM -> $262.21 fwd BVPS = $244.73, -28.9% vs CMP), Base $365.00 (50% prob: 13.0% ROAE -> 1.29x fwd BVPS), Bull $420.00 (20% prob: 15.0% ROAE, Casualty CR <99% -> 1.48x fwd BVPS).
web_blocks.if_off: If Casualty & Specialty combined ratio drops sustainably below 98% and Capital Partners quarterly fees rebound above $95M, sustainable ROAE rises toward 15.0% ($420+ value); if 10.0% ROAE (0.9333x P/B) collides with a +100 bps Treasury backup on 4.2-year bond duration (-$18/sh MTM hit), stressed fair value falls to $244.73 (-28.9% vs CMP), while Everest Group's 1.11x P/B implies ~$288 spot.

web_blocks.html: Decomposing RenaissanceRe's three earnings pillars illustrates why a 13.0% mid-cycle ROAE ceiling makes sense [1, 3, 18]. Underwriting must carry normal catastrophe budgets rather than 2026's 31.2% Property combined ratio, while Casualty & Specialty fights social inflation at 104.7% 9M CR [3, 12]. Investment float generates steady recurring NII ($1,703.5 million FY2025; $1,293.8 million 9M 2026), yet rate volatility on 4.2-year retained duration creates GAAP noise [1, 3]. Capital Partners fee income remains valuable ($258.9 million 9M 2026), but four straight quarters of fee compression cap valuation expansion [3, 18].

web_blocks.title: 7.2 Historical P/TBV Bands, Buyback Dilution Math & Duration Drag

web_blocks.html: Historical valuation bands confirm that $343.97 offers little cushion against cycle reversals [1, 18]. During the 2017–2022 soft market and catastrophe digestion years, RNR frequently traded at 0.90x to 1.10x book value [1]. Today's 1.32x P/B and 1.42x P/TBV multiples sit in the upper half of RenRe's decade corridor, right after a generational hard market peaked [3, 18, 21]. Share repurchases also work differently at 1.42x TBVPS than at 1.00x TBVPS. Retiring $1.0 billion of stock in 9M 2026 plus $143.8 million in October at $336.70/share boosts EPS because an 8.10x forward P/E represents a 12.3% earnings yield [3, 21]. Yet paying $1.42 for $1.00 of tangible equity trims TBVPS growth by roughly 1.5% to 2.5% annually [3, 18].

Rate sensitivity on the bond book adds another valuation cap [3, 18]. Extending retained fixed-income duration from 3.0 to 4.2 years boosted retained yield-to-maturity to 6.0%, but it triggered $(1,180.1) million in 9M 2026 trading-book MTM losses ($(879.8) million in Q3 alone) directly inside GAAP net income [3, 18]. Coupled with $1.60 billion in illiquid private credit funds and $3.86 billion in unfunded VIE commitments, investors must demand a wider valuation discount—not pay peak-cycle multiples—when underwriting 2027 [3].

web_blocks.title: 7.3 Peer Valuation Comparison: Listed Reinsurance & P&C Benchmarks

web_blocks.html: Cash-flow optics require the same normalization lens [1, 21]. Headline P/FCF of 4.93x looks optically cheap because audited FY2025 CFO ($3,693.1 million) included $1,288.7 million in float and reserve inflows from a quiet post-hard-market cash cycle [1, 21]. As gross premiums written shrink 13.4% YoY in 2026 and ceded retrocession climbs 20.1% YoY, net premium float inflows moderate naturally [3]. Normalizing FCF across catastrophe cycles confirms that 1.42x Q3 2026 TBVPS already prices fair intrinsic value [18, 23].

web_blocks.takeaway: RNR at 1.32x P/B (13.4% ROE) trades above Everest Group (1.11x P/B, 12.8% ROE) while sitting below higher-ROE peers Arch Capital (1.60x P/B, 18.7% ROE) and Travelers (2.78x P/B, 27.5% ROE).

web_blocks.html: Comparing RNR against listed P&C peers in our November 20, 2026 snapshot clarifies its relative pricing [21, 25, 26, 27]. Everest Group (EG, $15.63B market cap) trades at 1.11x P/B and 6.92x forward P/E on a 12.77% ROE and 10.60% ROIC, reflecting casualty reserve skepticism [25]. Arch Capital Group (ACGL, $35.42B) commands 1.60x P/B and 10.91x forward P/E because its mortgage-insurance mix sustains an 18.74% ROE and 16.35% ROIC with steadier underwriting margins [26]. Travelers (TRV, $80.63B) trades at 2.78x P/B and 12.68x forward P/E on a 27.50% ROE and 21.53% ROIC as a premier U.S. primary carrier [27].

RenaissanceRe sits right where its 13.44% trailing ROE and 11.22% ROIC belong: at 1.32x P/B (1.42x P/TBV) and 8.10x forward P/E [18, 21]. It carries conservative 0.21 Debt/Equity and a minimal 0.47% dividend yield ($1.63 TTM) to retain surplus [21, 22]. Yet unlike ACGL or TRV, RNR faces -21.18% TTM revenue contraction and -47.80% YoY quarterly sales drop as it prunes softening treaties, alongside -14.48% projected next-year EPS normalization [21]. Without clear relative mispricing versus EG or ACGL, RNR's valuation fails to justify new capital.
Valuation Trigger: Re-open underwriting only if shares fall toward $255 (1.05x Q3 TBVPS) or if Casualty CR drops below 99% alongside rising Capital Partners AUM and fees.

web_blocks.title: VALUATION VERDICT: FAIRLY PRICED WITH THIN ASYMMETRY
paragraphs: At $343.97 (1.42x Q3 TBVPS $242.51), RNR already prices a ~13.0% mid-cycle ROAE at a 10.5% cost of equity. Our $365.00 Base target (+6.1%) and $349.00 expected value (+1.5%, matching Finviz $349.94) leave less than 0.8:1 reward-to-risk against the $317.26 structural stop.

book_subsections.title: 7.1 Why Peak-Cycle Multiples Mislead in Reinsurance
paragraphs: If you glance quickly at RenaissanceRe's headline stock-screener ratios on November 20, 2026, it is easy to get fooled. At a closing price of $343.97, the stock trades at 9.89 times trailing earnings, 8.10 times forward earnings, and 4.93 times trailing free cash flow. Against a trailing twelve-month ROE of 13.44% and an annualized nine-month 2026 Operating ROACE of 20.3%, paying 1.32 times stated book value might look like a bargain. That trap is exactly how cyclical investors lose money.

In reinsurance, headline earnings multiples are lowest right near the peak of an underwriting cycle. Why? Because Wall Street knows that a 31.2% Property combined ratio—the unusually benign nine-month 2026 figure—will not last forever. In fact, consensus analyst estimates embedded in Finviz already project a 14.48% earnings contraction next year, and the average analyst target price sits at $349.94, barely 1.7% above today's $343.97 quote.

To cut through that noise, institutional insurance analysts throw away standard industrial cash-flow models and turn to the justified price-to-book framework: fair price-to-book equals normalized return on equity minus long-term growth, divided by the cost of equity minus long-term growth. Every input in that simple fraction forces you to confront reality rather than extrapolate a quiet hurricane season.

callouts.title: The Cyclical P/E Trap
callouts.text: An 8.10x forward P/E looks cheap only until Property Catastrophe losses revert from 31.2% back toward normal 55%–62% budgets and Casualty & Specialty drags on 110.6% Q3 combined ratios.

book_subsections.title: 7.2 Auditing Cost of Equity & Mid-Cycle ROAE (12%–14%)
paragraphs: Start with the denominator of our valuation model: the cost of equity. On November 19, 2026, the U.S. 10-year Treasury note yielded 5.04%, while the 2-year note stood at 4.76%. Some analysts argue that because RenaissanceRe has a stock-market beta of just 0.12, it deserves a low 8% or 9% cost of equity. That is a textbook mistake. Beta measures daily stock correlation to the S&P 500, not the risk of permanent capital loss when a Category 5 hurricane hits South Florida or when U.S. juries hand down nuclear casualty verdicts. Adding a realistic 5.46% catastrophe, duration, and reserve risk premium to a 5.04% risk-free yield sets our Cost of Equity at 10.50%.

Now look at the numerator: sustainable mid-cycle normalized ROAE. Our price-blind forensic audit of FY2025 and Q3 2026 filings revealed five concrete reasons why mid-cycle ROAE sits between 12.0% and 14.0%, centered around 13.0%, rather than repeating 2023–2025's 18.2% to 29.3% windfalls. First, property-catastrophe pricing softened in 2026 under abundant alternative ILS capital, prompting RenRe to cut Property Catastrophe gross premiums written by 19.9% year-over-year. Second, Casualty and Specialty—nearly 58% of FY2025 gross premiums—deteriorated to a 110.6% Q3 combined ratio with $54.66 million of adverse prior-year reserve development.

Third, Capital Partners quarterly fee income stepped down for four consecutive quarters, from $101.8 million in Q3 2025 to $81.7 million in Q3 2026, as third-party investors redeemed $649.2 million from DaVinciRe and $140.9 million from Fontana. Fourth, management stretched retained bond duration from 3.0 to 4.2 years on a trading-classified $25.20 billion bond portfolio, creating $1.18 billion of nine-month mark-to-market GAAP losses alongside $1.60 billion in locked-up private credit funds. Fifth, Bermuda's 15% Corporate Income Tax imposes a permanent tax drag, even with JV exclusions keeping FY2025 consolidated ETR at 9.9%, just as CFO Robert Qutub and CPO Ross Curtis retire at year-end 2026.

book_subsections.title: 7.3 The Math on $242.51 TBVPS & 12-Month Expected Value
paragraphs: Plugging a 13.0% mid-cycle ROAE (which equates to roughly 13.9% return on audited Q3 2026 tangible equity of $242.51 per share), a 10.50% cost of equity, and a 3.0% terminal growth rate into the justified P/B formula yields 1.333 times stated book value of $259.61—or $346.15 per share today. On tangible book value, 1.453 times $242.51 equals $352.45. Notice how tightly those numbers bracket today's $343.97 share price and Wall Street's $349.94 consensus target. The market is not mispricing RenaissanceRe; it is pricing a 13% mid-cycle return almost to the dollar.

Even if we project twelve months forward into Q3 2027, the math refuses to create an asymmetric bargain. Compounding $259.61 book value by +11.0% (13.0% ROAE minus 0.5% dividends and 1.5% buyback dilution at 1.42 times TBVPS) yields $288.17; subtracting ~200 basis points (~$5.17 per share) for fixed-maturity MTM drag and buyback-premium friction produces $283.00 Q3 2027E BVPS (+9.01%, or ~$267.50 TBVPS after scheduled intangibles amortization). Applying a 1.29x multiple yields our $365.00 Base Case fair value (+6.1%), and even unadjusted $288.17 at 1.29x ($371.74) still yields just 1.04-to-1 Base reward-to-risk at CMP. Weighting a 20% Bull Case at $420.00 (if Casualty CR falls below 99% and fees rebound) and a 30% Bear Case at $275.00 (if heavy catastrophes and casualty creep hit 10% ROAE) produces a probability-weighted expected value of $349.00, just +1.5% above CMP.

book_subsections.title: 7.4 Buyback Dilution at 1.42x TBVPS & Fixed-Income Duration Risk
paragraphs: Share buybacks deserve a closer look because many commentators treat all repurchases as equally magical. In FY2025, RenaissanceRe bought back $1.6 billion of stock, followed by $1.0 billion in nine-month 2026 and $143.8 million in October 2026 at $336.70 per share. When a reinsurer buys its own shares at 8.10 times forward earnings, earnings per share rise automatically. Yet buying back stock at 1.42 times tangible book value per share ($242.51) means paying $1.42 for $1.00 of tangible net assets, which shaves 1.5% to 2.5% off annual TBVPS compounding compared with buying below 1.00x book during soft-market troughs.

Duration extension on the investment portfolio introduces another layer of risk that pure P/B ratios hide. Unlike peers that tuck unrealized bond swings away inside Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income, RenRe marks its $25.20 billion fixed-maturity book directly through GAAP net income. Extending retained duration from 3.0 to 4.2 years locks in a healthy 6.0% yield-to-maturity if rates fall, but with 10-year Treasury yields sitting at 5.04%, any inflation flare-up hits quarterly GAAP earnings and net worth covenants immediately. Adding $3.86 billion of unfunded commitments to unconsolidated private fund VIEs underscores why demanding a wide margin of safety is essential.

book_subsections.title: 7.5 Peer Benchmarking: RNR vs. EG, ACGL & TRV
paragraphs: Stacking RenaissanceRe against the listed P&C and reinsurance peers in our November 20, 2026 snapshot removes any lingering illusion that RNR is deeply discounted. Everest Group (EG), at $421.98 and a $15.63 billion market cap, trades at 1.11 times book value and 6.92 times forward earnings on a 12.77% ROE. Arch Capital Group (ACGL), at $108.82 and a $35.42 billion market cap, commands 1.60 times book value and 10.91 times forward earnings because its diversified mortgage and specialty businesses earn an 18.74% ROE and 16.35% ROIC with less single-peril volatility. Travelers (TRV), at $393.43 and an $80.63 billion market cap, trades at 2.78 times book value on a towering 27.50% ROE.

RenaissanceRe's 1.32x book multiple (1.42x TBVPS) and 13.44% trailing ROE sit squarely in the middle of Everest and Arch—exactly where an insurer with elite property-cat modeling but a 110.6% Q3 casualty combined ratio and declining Capital Partners fees should trade. Because neither absolute excess-return math nor relative peer multiples reveal a compelling discount at $343.97, valuation fails to clear our hurdle for new capital.

callouts.quote: Fairly valued cyclical businesses in softening rate environments do not fail because they are bad companies; they fail the hurdle because paying 1.42x TBVPS leaves no margin for error.
callouts.author: Valuation Synthesis

book_subsections.title: 7.6 Cash Conversion Normalization & Why 4.93x P/FCF Is Not Cheap
paragraphs: Before leaving Chapter 7, we must address one final trap that catches value-oriented investors: RenaissanceRe's 4.93 times price-to-free-cash-flow ratio. In software or manufacturing, buying a business at under five times free cash flow is a generational gift. In property-catastrophe reinsurance, single-year cash flow can deceive you badly because premiums arrive upfront in cash while major catastrophe or casualty claims get paid out over three to ten years.

Look back at our audited FY2025 cash-flow waterfall in Chapter 3. Operating cash flow hit $3,693.1 million—with zero standalone capital expenditures—because $1,288.7 million of net reserve and float inflows rolled onto the balance sheet alongside elevated investment yields and relatively manageable catastrophe payouts. Now fast-forward to nine-month 2026. Gross premiums written fell 13.4% year-over-year, Property Catastrophe premiums dropped 19.9%, and ceded retrocessional premiums jumped 20.1% to $1,956.6 million. When premium volume shrinks and large casualty claims from social inflation and 2026 geopolitical loss events season into cash settlements, operating cash flow normalizes sharply lower.

That is why institutional insurance investors never anchor on trailing P/FCF. They anchor on tangible book value per share, normalized return on equity, and the spread between return on equity and cost of equity. At $343.97, paying 1.42 times audited Q3 2026 TBVPS ($242.51) for a business earning a 13.0% mid-cycle ROAE against a 10.50% cost of equity leaves almost zero structural discount. If you want true margin of safety in a cyclical reinsurer, you wait for 0.95x to 1.05x tangible book—roughly $230 to $255 per share—or wait for clear evidence that Casualty and Capital Partners fees have turned decisively higher.

book_subsections.title: 7.7 Dividend Retention vs. Capital-Return Reality
paragraphs: Management's capital-return mix reinforces the same valuation discipline. RenaissanceRe pays an annual dividend of just $1.63 per share—a tiny 0.47% yield representing 2.86% of trailing earnings—retaining more than 97% of profits inside the business. Compare that with Everest Group, which yields nearly four times as much on dividend payout, or Chubb and Travelers, which distribute steady cash dividends alongside buybacks. Retaining capital works wonders when an insurer either writes peak-rate catastrophe treaties at 25% expected ROEs or repurchases stock below tangible book value.

Yet in late 2026, neither high-return avenue is wide open. Property-catastrophe rates softened in 2026 under competing ILS supply, prompting RenRe to pull back capacity by nearly 20%. Simultaneously, its stock trades at 1.42 times tangible book value, so buybacks retire shares at a 42% premium to hard net assets. Under those conditions, retained capital earns solid but unspectacular mid-cycle returns—confirming once again why our valuation framework refuses to stretch above $365.00 in the Base Case.

book_subsections.title: 7.8 Stress-Testing Assumptions: What Would Make Us Wrong on Value?
paragraphs: Every valuation model is only as honest as its falsification triggers. Let us walk through exactly what would make our $365.00 Base Case and $349.00 expected value too conservative—and what would make them too generous. On the upside, suppose the 2027 Atlantic hurricane season turns out unusually quiet, Casualty and Specialty combined ratios drop cleanly below 99% because recent general-liability rate hikes earn through ahead of jury inflation, and Capital Partners reverses its four-quarter fee slide back above $350 million annually. In that Bull Case, sustainable ROAE lifts toward 15.0%, justifying roughly 1.48 to 1.60 times book value, or $420 per share.

Now weigh the symmetrical downside risk. Suppose 2027 brings a normal-to-active North Atlantic catastrophe season just as January 1 and June 1 property-catastrophe treaty renewals soften another 10% to 15%, while U.S. social inflation forces another round of adverse general-liability actuarial assumption changes above 106% combined ratio. Layer on a rate shock hitting RenRe's 4.2-year retained fixed-income trading book. In our baseline Bear Case, ROAE compresses to 10.0% at 1.00 times book value ($275 per share, -20.1%). Under an even sharper combined stress—where 10.0% ROAE (0.9333x justified P/B) coincides with a +100-basis-point Treasury backup cutting forward BVPS growth to +1.0% ($262.21)—fair value drops to $244.73, a -28.9% drawdown from $343.97.

When your Bear Case carries -20% downside at 30% probability, your Bull Case carries +22% upside at 20% probability, and your Base Case offers +6% upside at 50% probability, the expected value math locks at +1.5%. Passing on +1.5% expected value at 1.42 times tangible book value is not pessimism; it is basic arithmetic.

book_subsections.title: 7.9 Reconciling Book Value, Tangible Book Value & Validus Intangibles
paragraphs: One forensic detail from our filing audit explains why checking tangible book value per share ($242.51) alongside stated book value per share ($259.61) changes valuation precision. The $17.10 per share gap reflects $587.1 million of goodwill and intangible assets sitting on the September 30, 2026 balance sheet: $362.8 million from Validus Re, $200.1 million from Platinum Underwriters, and $24.2 million from Tokio Millennium Re.

Because Value of Business Acquired (VOBA) from Validus Re finished amortizing at year-end 2025 and remaining intangibles amortize smoothly ($71.1 million in FY2025 and $61.3 million expected in FY2026), stated book value slowly converges toward tangible book value. At $343.97, paying 1.42 times hard tangible equity means investors are paying a 42% premium over liquid reinsurance capital—leaving zero margin if catastrophe losses or casualty reserve charges erode surplus.

Notice one more implication of that $17.10 per share intangible wedge. When analysts quote RenaissanceRe at 1.32 times stated book value, they include $587.1 million of acquisition goodwill and intangibles that cannot pay a single dollar of hurricane or casualty claims. Stripping those intangibles out leaves $242.51 per share of hard tangible equity—putting the live price at 1.42 times tangible book value.

Across global reinsurance peers, 1.42 times tangible book value is a full multiple whenever property-catastrophe rates are softening and casualty reserves require active assumption strengthening. Wait until Mr. Market offers either a deeper discount near 1.05 times tangible book ($255 per share) or unambiguous earnings proof that mid-cycle ROAE belongs closer to 15% than 13%.
